Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Pakistan's reply. The umpires are out in the middle. Bangladesh players are seen in a huddle near the ropes before taking their respective field positions. Azan Awais and Imam-ul-Haq are the two openers for Pakistan. Taskin Ahmed will start with the new ball. Let's go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

The tail folded quickly as well - The second session barely got going before the curtains fell on the Bangladeshi innings. Right after the Lunch break, the set Mushfiqur Rahim was dismissed in the very first over for a gritty 71. Taskin Ahmed added valuable runs towards the end, and Bangladesh were eventually bundled out for a massive 413 runs. It was a fantastic first-innings batting effort from the hosts, setting up daunting scoreboard pressure for the visitors. Mohammad Abbas was the pick of the bowlers, finishing with a five-wicket haul, while Shaheen Afridi chipped in with three wickets. Now, the pressure is entirely on the Pakistan batters to respond.

Abbas with the fightback for Pakistan - Pakistan finally found some life on the morning of Day 2. Coming out with clear intent, the pacers hit the right lengths and tested the Bangladeshi batters. The veteran Mushfiqur Rahim remained rock solid, calmly bringing up his fifty, but his partners couldn't stick around. Mohammad Abbas was the absolute star of the morning session, bagging three crucial wickets to keep the scoring in check. By Lunch, Bangladesh were 380/7, with Pakistan finally clawing their way back into the contest.

The Tigers dominated Day 1 - It was a proper old-school Test match on Day 1 in Mirpur! Pakistan struck early with the new ball, leaving Bangladesh looking very shaky at 31/2. But then, Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mominul Haque completely flipped the script. They stitched together a monstrous 170-run partnership that frustrated the Pakistani bowlers all day long. Shanto hammered a brilliant 101, while Mominul fell heartbreakingly short of his century on 91. Bangladesh finished the opening day in total control at 301/4.

Bangladesh 380/7 - At the Lunch break, Bangladesh are 380 for 7, with Rahim holding the key to how much further the hosts can push their first-innings total in the afternoon session. We will be back with the post-Lunch session at 6.40 am GMT. Stay tuned...

Mushfiqur stands tall - Despite the flurry of wickets at the other end, Mushfiqur Rahim remains the anchor for Bangladesh. He looks well-set on 71, eyeing a significant three-figure mark as he nears a century. However, his progress depends heavily on finding a reliable partner, as the tumbling wickets have left the tail exposed.

Lower-order struggle - The Bangladeshi lower order has struggled to weather the storm as Abbas continues to strike. Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Taijul Islam manage to add a few useful runs to the total, yet neither could survive the disciplined wrath of Abbas. By the end of the session, Abbas has claimed all three wickets to fall, adding to his solo wicket on Day 1, standing alone as the only bowler with the necessary bite to trouble the opposition. The rest of the Pakistan bowling unit struggles to find their rhythm, leaving the heavy lifting entirely to their premier seamer.

Abbas dominates the morning session - Resuming at an overnight score of 301 for 4, Bangladesh starts the day with intent, keeping the scoreboard ticking at a healthy rate. However, the momentum shifted as Mohammad Abbas asserted his dominance, proving to be the standout performer in the Pakistani bowling attack. Litton Das looked fluid and composed during his stay at the crease, but he eventually fell victim to Abbas’s relentless accuracy. Abbas continued his clinical display throughout the morning, consistently outclassing his fellow bowlers who appear to be operating several levels below his standard.
LUNCH ON DAY 2 - A total of 24 overs were bowled with Bangladesh scoring 79 runs for the loss of 3 wickets in this session.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the play to begin on Day 2. Mushfiqur Rahim and Litton Das have walked out in the middle to resume their innings for Bangladesh. It will be Hasan Ali to bowl the first over of the day.

PITCH REPORT ON DAY 2 - Athar Ali Khan reports that the pitch remains quite green, though cracks have opened up slightly more since the previous day, potentially targeting the off stump for left-handers and the leg stump for right-handers. Khan notes that the variable bounce that troubled batters on Day 1 will likely persist, accompanied by some lateral movement off the surface. With an average of 265 runs and 12 wickets typically seen on Day 2 at this venue, Athar reckons all bowlers, whether seamers or spinners, should maintain a disciplined attack on the stumps.

Bangladesh batter, Mominul Haque is up for a chat - Mominul Haque says that while the opening session was challenging on Day 1, the surface eventually became excellent for batting as the ball began coming onto the bat nicely. Mominul Haque acknowledges that Test pitches often change drastically based on evolving weather and environmental conditions. Despite falling short of a century, Mominul feels good about his contribution, stating he feels no guilt or disappointment because he is thankful for every run scored. Looking at the bigger picture, Mominul Haque highlights the squad's steady improvement over the last few years, attributing their success to a strong team bond and a clear understanding of individual roles within the side.

The crucial first hour - Grab your coffee, because the first hour of play will dictate the entire rhythm of the day and this match, to some extent. Will the second new ball finally dance for Pakistan's frustrated pacers, or will Mushfiqur's calm, old-school Test match temperament continue to build an insurmountable wall? It's the ultimate morning battle of early movement versus quiet confidence, and you won't want to miss a single delivery.

Pakistan’s desperate hunt - For the visitors, the morning is all about early breakthroughs with the relatively new ball. Pakistan's pace attack didn't bowl terribly yesterday, but a glaring lack of discipline, highlighted by 32 agonizing extras and a parade of no-balls, let the momentum slip away. Shaheen Afridi, Hasan Ali, and Abbas need to strike immediately and plug the leaks before the hosts completely break their spirits.

The host's eye a monster total - Bangladesh enters the morning session with a clear, ruthless objective, to bat Pakistan completely out of the game. With the veteran Mushfiqur Rahim steadily marching toward a half-century and the ever-capable Litton Das anchoring the other end, expect the Tigers to confidently target 400. The longer they occupy the crease, the heavier the scoreboard pressure will become on a pitch that is already slowing down.

Welcome to Day 2 in Mirpur! Welcome back to what promises to be a thrilling Day 2 of this classic test match. After an opening day defined by Bangladeshi grit and a frustrating mountain of Pakistani extras, the hosts are firmly in the driver's seat at 301/4. Najmul Hossain Shanto’s dazzling 101 and Mominul Haque’s heartbreakingly brilliant 91 have perfectly set the stage, turning early morning jitters into absolute dominance.

That's a wrap from Day 1 - Right then, that is it from the opening day of this Test, where Bangladesh firmly seized control of the contest, while Pakistan will be desperate for early breakthroughs on Day 2. Action resumes on Saturday, 9th May at 4 am GMT, and you can join us a little earlier for all the build-up. Until then, cheers!

Pakistan run out of answers - The final session followed a similar pattern, with Bangladesh tightening their grip on the game through another dominant batting effort. Mominul Haque remained solid and added a fluent 75-run stand with Mushfiqur Rahim before falling for 91, just short of a deserved ton. Pakistan's bowlers rarely troubled the batters, with Noman Ali leaking runs despite picking up a wicket and also struggling with his run-up, bowling multiple No-Balls. Even the second new ball brought little success as Mushfiqur and Litton Das safely saw out the session, with Rahim staying unbeaten on 48.

Shanto century caps dominant session - The second session belonged entirely to Bangladesh as Shanto and Mominul stitched together a superb 170-run partnership that completely shifted the momentum of the game. The duo frustrated Pakistan's bowlers on a flattening surface, rotating strike consistently while punishing anything loose. Shanto eventually brought up a brilliant century before Mohammad Abbas finally broke the stand right before Tea, but Bangladesh still headed into the break firmly in control.

Bangladesh rebuild after early collapse - Pakistan made the perfect start after opting to bowl first in Mirpur, reducing Bangladesh to 31/2 inside the opening hour with Shaheen Afridi and Hasan Ali striking early. However, once the new-ball threat faded, Bangladesh slowly settled in. Najmul Hossain Shanto absorbed the pressure beautifully and began counterattacking, while Mominul Haque played the anchor's role in a crucial rebuilding phase.

SESSION SUMMARY - 100 runs, 1 wicket in 32 overs! A day that belonged completely to Bangladesh after being asked to bat first in Mirpur, scoring 100 runs or more in each session to take complete control of the contest. Despite the early blows, they showed immense composure to recover strongly and move into a commanding position. It was a tough day out for Pakistan, and while the decision to field first may already be proving costly, they will still hope for quick wickets on Day 2 to pull things back.

... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

A centurion falls - Bangladesh reached 201 for 3 in 53 overs at Tea, with Mominul Haque on 64 and Shanto getting his maiden century against Pakistan and his ninth test hundred. The third-wicket partnership has been the backbone of the day, completely absorbing Pakistan's threat and turning the momentum firmly in Bangladesh's favour. But just after the century of Shanto, Pakistan found a way to break the partnership, and it was through Mohammad Abbas. However, Musfiqur Rahim replaced his skipper and is yet to open his account. It will be interesting to see how the Pakistan bowlers will react in the last session on Day 1, but Bangladesh have a strong grasp after the end of the afternoon session. We will be back with the post-Tea break at 8.40 am GMT​​​​​​.

The partnership that set the game - The partnership continued to flourish as both batters moved into the second half of their respective innings. Haque brought up his fifty in composed fashion. He looked particularly elegant on the back foot as he produced some delightful ramp shots over the slip cordon. Shanto, meanwhile, grew increasingly fluent at the other end, rotating the strikes and punishing anything overpitched or loose short deliveries with authority.

Steady start for the afternoon session - Bangladesh resumed after the Lunch break at 101 for 2 after 26 overs, with Najmul Hossain Shanto unbeaten on 39 and Mominul Haque steady on 31. Pakistan came out with renewed intent in the second session by bowling back-to-back maiden overs, but the batters did well to control their nerves. Shanto set the tone early by punishing the short deliveries from the pacers.
TEA on DAY 1 - 27 overs were bowled in this session, with Bangladesh scoring 100 runs and losing 1 wicket.

Discipline or dominance - As they head into the afternoon session, Shan Masood’s men must find a way to dry up the runs and force an error, or they risk letting the game slip further away before the first day is out. The Pakistani bowlers need to be much more disciplined to curtail the flow of runs first, which might just create the pressure needed to break this burgeoning partnership. We will be back with the post-Lunch session at 6.40 am GMT​​​​​​.

Pakistan's inconsistent opening salvo - For Pakistan, the morning has been a case of hot and cold spells. While Hasan Ali struck gold with a wicket on his very first delivery, he has struggled to maintain that threat. Shaheen Afridi’s radar was wayward throughout his opening burst, and while Mohammad Abbas maintained his trademark discipline in the corridor of uncertainty, his lack of pace failed to hurry the Bangladeshi batters on this surface.

The captain’s stand and Mominul’s composure - Since those breakthroughs, captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and the experienced Mominul Haque have slammed that door shut with a rock-solid, unbeaten 70-run partnership for the third wicket. Shanto has looked particularly fluent, racing to 39 with authoritative strokeplay, while Mominul has provided the perfect foil, reaching 31 with a composed approach. The duo appears set for a long haul, capitalising on a Pakistani bowling effort that has been largely inconsistent.

Resilience amidst uneven bounce - At the Lunch break on Day 1 in Mirpur, Bangladesh, sit comfortably at 101/2, having successfully navigated a tricky opening session after being put in to bat. Despite the visible grass cover and unpredictable, uneven bounce that promised to make life a nightmare for the batters, the hosts have largely neutralised Pakistan's much-vaunted pace attack. Openers Shadman Islam and Mahmudul Hasan Joy did the heavy lifting early on, weathering a difficult new-ball spell, however, just as they looked to accelerate, both fell in quick succession, leaving the door slightly ajar for the visitors.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the play to begin. The two umpires have already taken their positions just after the national anthems. The players of Pakistan have scattered and Shaheen Afridi is walking towards his bowling mark with the red cherry in his hands. For Bangladesh, it's Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Shadman Islam to open the innings. Hassan Joy to take the strike. Away we go...

We are moments away from the start of the game, but before that, the players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for the respective national anthems. It will be the away team, Pakistan's first, followed by that of Bangladesh.

A green deck - Athar Ali Khan provides the pitch report, highlighting that this ground has recently been a productive venue for the hosts, who have secured three wins in their last five Tests here. He observes that while there is visible grass on a good length to hold the surface together, the track appears to be one where batters can find their rhythm and score freely once they are well-set at the crease. Noting the morning conditions, he anticipates that the first hour will be key for the bowlers to exploit any early moisture or assistance provided by that live grass.

Skipper of Bangladesh - Najmul Hossain Shanto reckons the pitch looks good, like the ones they've had in recent ODIs. Najmul adds that he's happy with the seamers, especially with Taskin's back and with Nahid Rana doing well. Shanto concludes, saying this series is important, playing at home, and the team is excited to do something special.

Skipper of Pakistan - Shan Masood reckons that the Mirpur conditions align with their expectations and justify their versatile squad selection. Shan presses on the need for a strong start to build momentum for the series, opting to focus on a daily progression rather than looking too far ahead. Masood informs that they have two highly anticipated debutants, opener Azan Awais, who has been a consistent domestic performer who has transitioned from the Under-19 ranks, and Abdullah Fazal, who earns his spot following a standout Player of the Match performance in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy. Shan also expresses disappointment over the absence of star batter Babar Azam, who misses out due to a late injury risk.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Mahmudul Hasan Joy, Shadman Islam, Mominul Haque, Mushfiqur Rahim, Litton Das (WK), Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Taijul Islam, Taskin Ahmed, Nahid Rana, Ebadot Hossain.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Azan Awais (On debut), Imam-ul-Haq, Abdullah Fazal (On debut), Shan Masood (C), Saud Shakeel, Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Salman Agha, Shaheen Afridi, Noman Ali, Hasan Ali, Mohammad Abbas.
TOSS - ​​Pakistan have won the coin flip and they will be BOWLING first.

The Dhaka surface - The Mirpur pitch has raised eyebrows with its grassy appearance, a departure from the traditional low-and-slow turning tracks of Dhaka, as per the first look before the game. This could offer significant seam movement and bounce during the first three days, potentially playing into the hands of Pakistan's seamers and Bangladesh's returning pace duo. With scattered thunderstorms also forecast for the third day, the ability to capitalize on windows of dry play will be essential for both captains in their pursuit of critical WTC points. Toss and team news in a bit.

Strategic strengths - Their primary challenge, however, remains the fragility of the top-order batting for Bangladesh. They must provide a substantial scoreboard cushion to allow their bowlers to dictate terms. A repeat of past collapses against high-quality seamers could prove fatal. Pakistan, on the other hand, boasts a more versatile bowling attack that balances raw pace with the crafty spin of Sajid Khan and Noman Ali, both of whom are well-equipped to exploit any kind of wear and tear of a Dhaka surface. Pakistan’s greatest hurdle is their internal stability. With a new coaching regime under immense scrutiny and a recent history of erratic Test performances, they must find a way to maintain discipline over five grueling days. Success for the visitors hinges on their ability to strike early with the new ball and prevent Bangladesh's middle order from settling into a rhythm.

Clash of tactical philosophies - Tactically, the battle will hinge on the adaptability of each side's strengths. Bangladesh will lean heavily on their spin-bowling core, led by the vastly experienced Mehidy Hasan Miraz and Taijul Islam, to exploit local conditions. However, the visitors must contend with the significant late news that star batter Babar Azam will miss the first Test due to an injury to his left knee, placing immense pressure on the rest of the lineup. Pakistan’s pace attack, historically their primary weapon, will look to capitalize on any early movement, while Bangladesh’s revamped batting order must prove they can build substantial totals under pressure. The hosts' captain, Najmul Hossain Shanto, is himself recovering from a hamstring strain but is expected to lead the side as they attempt to replicate their 2-0 form from the Ireland series last November.

Quest for dominance - Hello and welcome to all the fans tuning in. This two-Test series between Bangladesh and Pakistan is framed by a fascinating shift in their recent red-ball hierarchy. While Pakistan has historically dominated this matchup, the landscape shifted dramatically in late 2024 when Bangladesh secured a landmark 2-0 whitewash on Pakistani soil. That victory remains a cornerstone of the hosts' psychological edge as they prepare to defend their turf in Dhaka. Bangladesh's chief selector, Habibul Bashar, has publicly called for an attacking approach, evidenced by the inclusion of uncapped top-order batter Tanzid Hasan and first-class standout Amite Hasan, fueling their ambition to solidify their status as a rising powerhouse in Asian Test conditions. Conversely, Pakistan arrives under a cloud of transition and pressure, with captain Shan Masood leading a squad that must reconcile the brilliance of veterans like Babar Azam and Shaheen Afridi with a dire need for consistency. For the visitors, this series is not just about points in the World Test Championship, but a critical mission to restore their wounded pride against an opponent that no longer fears them.
